di est formaliter pretium, quatenus numera-
tur à persolvente, & acceptatur ab eo, cui

non & persolvatur nomine captivi, & acce-

2. Falsum est solam Dei vo-
luntatem esse causam, cur vis meriti non per-
tingat ad reprobos: est enim sola causa prima
& remota: at reproborum malitiosa rejectio
Christi est causa proxima, quâ admirandâ
confociatione ipsorum obstinatus animus liber-
tate id respuat & amplecti nolit, quod abso-
luta Dei voluntas ad ipsos pertinere nollet, &
quoniam libere indulgent infidelitati suæ, ju-
re meritissimo plectuntur.
3. Cupimus, ut
nos doceant, quid commeritus sit Christus re-
probis? Non fidem, non regenerationem:
id enim ipsi respuunt p.95 [?]. c.8. nimirum com-
meritus est iis ut possint credere vel non crede-
re, id quod ab instinctu humani arbitrii esse cre-
dunt, siquidem sincere agere didicissent.
5. Pro-
ponatur à Deo, Iudæ, Simoni Mago, aliisque re-
probis universal. promissio: Intendo & decerno
vobis salutem, si credideritis in filium meum. Illud

dubia erit Dei scientia, quod absurdum. Si ad

page.notes: The first line begins with a fragment, "ctionem", whose opening letters are cut off at the top of the scan. The page number is printed with a final digit that looks like a long-s form; read as 263. The reference "p.95" is doubtful: the 5 is printed in a form resembling ʃ, so it is marked [?]. Greek λύτρον is transcribed from the print; its accents are not fully certain. The line ending "ex-" is cut off by the page foot, so the word continues on the next page.
